claims.text: Conventionally processed alloys such as NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 or TiVNbTa may exhibit a uniformly brittle continuous-B2 or coarse microstructure.
Optimized hot rolling followed by rapid annealing can transform the candidate alloy into an inverted dual-phase microstructure.
The targeted inverted microstructure consists of a continuous BCC matrix containing finely dispersed nanoscale B2 precipitates.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix is associated with high yield strength but poor room-temperature ductility in two-phase refractory HEAs.

Inverting the phase topology to a continuous BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates improves room-temperature compressive ductility while maintaining high yield strength at room and elevated temperatures.
Increasing Hf content raises yield strength without reducing plasticity at room and elevated temperatures.
Combining the inverted phase topology with increased Hf will improve both yield strength and room-temperature tensile ductility relative to conventional processing.
The modified alloy will retain high-temperature strength up to approximately 1200 °C.
The modified alloy will preserve irradiation stability during He-ion irradiation at about 1023 K and fluences up to 3×10^16 ions/cm².
Discrete B2 precipitates act as uniformly distributed obstacles to dislocation motion without compromising overall ductility.
Grain refinement and phase stability limit irradiation-induced defect clustering and swelling.
Controlled Hf addition promotes solid-solution strengthening.
Controlled Hf addition improves microstructural stability during thermal exposure and irradiation.
The proposed dual-phase microstructure will resist irradiation-induced degradation and grain coarsening better than conventionally processed alloys.
Standard single-phase or continuous-B2 refractory HEAs typically combine high strength with poor ductility.
Conventionally processed baseline alloys are prone to irradiation-induced phase instability or grain coarsening.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires increased Hf content, but the experiment describes the conventional and tailored sets as having identical compositions while also assigning slight Hf enhancement to the tailored set.
